transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-03-19
Time: 15:00 UTC
Duration: ~48 minutes
Location: Zoom
Attendees: Sofia Ramirez (Redwood AE), Ethan Cole (Redwood CSM), Maya Patel (Redwood SE), Dana Lee (Astrid Head of ML), Markus Voss (Astrid Platform), Leah Ortiz (Astrid Procurement)

Summary:
High-level Q1 review: usage growth is steady (~28% QoQ), cost creep on multi-turn chat routes observed, one outage incident in Jan tied to a model rollout (KV cache invalidation) discussed; Astrid is evaluating Dedicated capacity vs. staying on hosted due to latency SLOs for a new realtime assistant. Action items and next steps agreed at the end.

Topics covered:
- Usage/consumption trends and cost drivers
- Reliability incidents and mitigations (Jan outage, fallback behavior)
- Roadmap alignment: Dedicated vs Hosted, VPC/private deployment timeline, RBAC and audit log requirements
- Performance baseline: batching, quantization, and sequence length impact
- Procurement and contract questions

Transcript:
[00:00] Sofia: hey everybody, thanks for joining. quick intros \u000E2\u0004\u001A we'll go through Q1 numbers, reliability notes, and then ops items. Dana, want to kick off with how things are feeling on your side?
[00:18] Dana: yeah, thanks. overall things are good, usage up, but we're seeing some cost surprises on the multi-turn chat, especially the customer_support route. tokens per convo spiked in feb. we ran into a higher-than-expected tail for sequence lengths.
[00:35] Markus: and to add, latency was fine for most traffic but we did have that Jan incident where a model rollback caused increased 95th pct latency for about 20 minutes, which triggered alerts. We followed the fallback to small-model policy but it still impacted response time for some users.
[00:55] Maya: can you remind me which model version that was? was it the 7B quantized profile?
[01:03] Dana: i think it was redwood-7b-q4a-v2? transcription may mislabel that. our engineers saw large KV cache misses after the rollout.
[01:20] Ethan: thanks, that's helpful. just to frame, our ops team identified the KV invalidation during rollouts as an edge case for that model family; we've put a mitigation pattern in the runbook. we'll share the exact steps.
[01:35] Leah: on procurement \u000E2\u0004\u001A cost is the big question. if you move to Dedicated what are the delta numbers, like headroom and savings for high-volume routes?
[01:48] Sofia: good question. high level: Dedicated gives you predictable throughput and per-token effective unit cost drops about 15-35% depending on utilization and batching. but there's an up-front reserved commit. we'll send a tailored pricing sheet after we see your route distribution.
[02:10] Dana: sounds good. we need throughput guarantees for sub-400ms p95 on our realtime assistant route. hosted's been borderline during peak.
[02:22] Maya: for p95 sub-400ms, we usually recommend a dedicated pool with burst and prefix caching enabled, plus an aggressive batching policy for non-realtime routes. we can also recommend quantization profiles \u000E2\u0004\u001A q4f and int8 hybrids \u000E2\u0004\u001A depending on your accuracy tolerance.
[02:44] Markus: what about our SSO/SAML and audit log requirements? that's a gating factor for Private deployment.
[02:52] Sofia: we support SSO/SAML and logged audit trails today; the Private option adds customer-managed KMS integration and higher retention SLAs for logs. we'll attach our SOC 2 and security kit.
[03:08] Dana: perfect. can you also outline the upgrade path from Hosted -> Dedicated -> Private? timeline and migrations steps?
[03:16] Ethan: Quick overview: you can start hosted, add dedicated pools for critical routes (no-app-change), then migrate to Private with a control-plane handover and network peering. migration typically takes 4-8 weeks depending on firewall/KMS work. we'll provide a detailed migration checklist.
[03:40] Dana: one more on reliability \u000E2\u0004\u001A can you run a canary with our staging traffic to validate the KV behavior? we want to avoid a repeat.
[03:49] Maya: yes, we can schedule a baseline run. ideally we get your sequence distribution and sample prompt set; we'll run 3 load profiles (low/med/high) and capture latency, kv hit rate, and memory churn.
[04:05] Markus: our ops can extract the sequence histograms and top-100 prompts, i can send that by end of week.
[04:13] Leah: procurement timeline \u000E2\u0004\u001A we are looking at a decision window by mid-April if numbers look right.
[04:20] Sofia: noted \u000E2\u0004\u001A we'll prioritize the pricing and baseline.
[04:28] [---brief cross talk, minor audio glitch---]
[05:10] Sofia: digging into costs, Dana \u000E2\u0004\u001A do you have a breakdown by route? is most spend on customer_support or on the analytics ingestion?
[05:18] Dana: customer_support + notification generation is the main cost. analytics embedding jobs are actually offloaded to a separate vector-db pipeline, but we do have embedding spikes after product launches.
[05:29] Maya: for the chat routes, caching prefixes for support templates typically knocks down token counts 20-40% if you can centralize boilerplate. Also recommend response truncation for tokens beyond 512 for non-critical messages.
[05:48] Markus: any docs you can share for that optimization?
[05:52] Sofia: yes, we'll attach the Optimize playbook and a sample prompt set mapping doc.
[06:05] Dana: curious about quality regressions with quantization \u000E2\u0004\u001A our product team is wary of int8 impacting answer fidelity.
[06:13] Maya: fair. our recommended approach is tiered: q4f on high-precision routes and int8/hybrid on backfill or notification routes. we run A/B evals on your prompt set to measure delta; usually fidelity drop is minimal for many use cases, but we'll measure for you.
[06:31] Dana: that's exactly what we need.
[06:35] Sofia: switching to reliability \u000E2\u0004\u001A Jan incident root cause recap: rollout triggered a cache reinitialization and some requests hit the fallback model instead of the warmed shard. we've added a pre-warm step and a canary window in the deployment pipeline.
[06:51] Markus: excellent, can we get those runbook steps? we need to align with our on-call flow.
[06:57] Ethan: will share the runbook and we can walk through on the staging test next week.
[07:05] Leah: procurement \u000E2\u0004\u001A are there any minimums for Dedicated?
[07:10] Sofia: minimum commit varies by region; typical is 3-month minimum for burst-enabled pools, annual for best pricing. we'll include both options in the proposal.
[07:22] Dana: on roadmap alignment \u000E2\u0004\u001A we have a multi-release plan to expand realtime assistant to 75% of customers by Q4. we need confidence on latency and costs to commit.
[07:34] Maya: that's doable. we'll model cost at scale once we have your sequence and concurrency distributions, and run a runway forecast to show cost/kg tokens vs hosted.
[07:47] Markus: how do rollbacks and model variants interplay with deductions on the billing side? we had confusion with multi-model fallback counts.
[07:56] Sofia: billing is by token consumed per request; fallbacks are recorded as metadata. we can add a per-route accounting sheet so you can see fallback token delta and assign to the correct cost center.
[08:10] Dana: great.
[08:15] [longer discussion, demo links and docs referenced]
[08:45] Sofia: quick recap and next steps \u000E2\u0004\u001A i'll send the dedicated pricing + runbook + security kit by Monday 2026-03-23. Maya will run a baseline test on staging and share results by 2026-03-26. Dana/Markus will share prompt/sequence artifacts by 2026-03-24. Ethan will schedule the follow-up check-in in ~90 days.
[09:10] Leah: thanks all. any procurement docs we should prepare on our side?
[09:15] Leah: i'll prepare an internal cost comparison template and share with Sofia.
[09:22] Sofia: perfect. thanks everyone, we'll follow up with the artifacts.

End of transcript.
